excerpt: You send your oil to the sea through a pipeline across a neighbour, and you are connecting hundreds of thousands of citizens to power each year.
paras: You send your oil to the sea through a pipeline across a neighbour, and you are connecting hundreds of thousands of citizens to power each year. Almost half of you are children, and on the last measure nine in ten could not read by the end of primary school. Let the oil teach and light every one of them.

Your partners have returned to the table. In October 2026 the International Monetary Fund reached a staff-level agreement on a new programme of $203 million. In March 2026 the World Bank approved a $250 million grant to widen access to finance for your small firms, after $220 million in 2025 for food security and essential services. Its projects for electricity, including the Kandadji dam, total $1.2 billion.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Only six in every hundred of you cook with clean fuel, and about one in five has electricity. Only nine in every hundred of you have safely managed sanitation. At the last count, in 2019, ninety in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Clean energy sets your Coverage today, at 6 out of 100, with sanitation and reading close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Niger: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Nigerien falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: Half of you are children. Let every barrel buy a classroom and a light.
